NPS_FOBU12018.title: National Park Service Fossil Butte: Lygodium kaulfussi FOBU12018
NPS_FOBU12018.notes: Official specimen record labels fossil4.8cm tall. Two elongate blunt lobes and small attached fertile structure visible. Modern climbing fern ecology on page is not direct wholeplant fossil evidence.
NPS_FOBU12018.inspection: Actual full NPS photo personally viewed before concept: broad two-lobed blade, deep cleft, small branched fertile tuft at narrow convergence; no complete climbing axis or roots.

MANCHESTER_ZAVADA1987.title: Manchester and Zavada1987 Lygodium foliage with intact sorophores from the Eocene of Wyoming
MANCHESTER_ZAVADA1987.notes: Original author-uploaded primary full text read at ResearchGate245502765. Fossil dimorphic fertile and sterile foliage physically connected. Modern L.palmatum comparison is not identity. Direct article plate pixels inaccessible; actual morphology photo is NPS. No claim exact cast or microscopic sorangial reconstruction.
MANCHESTER_ZAVADA1987.inspection: Primary text read; original article pixels not acquired. NPS original specimen photo supplies actual pixel evidence.

WAN2020_LAB.title: Wan etal2020 Flabellophyton study, authors State Key Laboratory institutional report
WAN2020_LAB.notes: Primary author institutional report and actual composite figure. Flabellophyton Ediacaran thallus has close unbranched radial filaments, narrow stalk and small basal holdfast; affinity unresolved. Model compressed fossil-style narrowfan rather than claiming living conic volume. Far-right reconstruction separated from fossil photos.
WAN2020_LAB.inspection: Personally read report and viewed full600px institutional image: left Lantian fossil compressions elongated narrow fans with fine channels and slender base. Other panels and far-right living reconstruction not used as measured fossil shape.

WAN2020_PRIMARY.title: Wan etal2020 The evolution of the macroalgal genus Flabellophyton and its paleogeographic and paleoecological significance
WAN2020_PRIMARY.notes: GondwanaResearch84:296-314 original preproof text read through BSIP indexed PDF. Closely bundled unbranched filaments radiate from basal attachment; proposed live cone is hypothesis. Direct BSIP fetch502 and screenshot unavailable, so no false originalplatepixel claim.
WAN2020_PRIMARY.inspection: Primary relevant systematic text read; institutional figure actually inspected separately.

DAWSON1888.title: J.W.Dawson1888 The Geological History of Plants Fig16B and bilobata description
DAWSON1888.notes: Original author historical illustration Fig16B only: small oval/reniform bilobed bodies with rounded prominences and central depression. Do not adopt obsolete waterfern/sporocarp assignment, or microscopic contents depicted in other panels. Modern identity remains uncertain.
DAWSON1888.inspection: Personally viewed actual original Fig16 raster: B is uppermiddle three oval bodies, first has two rounded lobes divided by shallow central groove. Not A,C,D,E. Illustration not fossil photograph.

SCHOPF1970.title: Schopf and Schwietering1970 The Foerstia Zone of the Ohio and Chattanooga Shales
SCHOPF1970.notes: USGS Bulletin1294H original full text read via web indexedPDF, including plate1 caption bilateral and infolded-groove specimens. DirectPDF403 and screenshotcachemiss; no pixel claim. Later uncertainty retained rather than assert original algal assignment.
SCHOPF1970.inspection: Primary text and original captions read, plate pixels unavailable.

NAPLES2013.title: Naples paleobotanical museum fossil collection Delpinoa50-51 pp61-83, Fig6c
NAPLES2013.notes: Actual fossil photograph supplemental only. Page66Fig6c dark oval carbonaceous body, bilobed contour not clearly resolved. Article notes disputed affinity. Museum age label conflicts with typical UpperDevonian record and is not used for precise age.
NAPLES2013.inspection: Printed66 actual rendered fullpage personally inspected. Fig6c alone, no invented tiny outlines from its lowcontrast pixels.

WHITFIELD1894.title: Whitfield1894 On new forms of marine algae from the Trenton Limestone, PlateXI11-13
WHITFIELD1894.notes: Original BulletinAMNH6:351-358 downloaded and read. PlateXI11 primary upright featherlike plume, little sideways plume on another shale layer NOT attached branch. Fig12 depicts whorls. Old isolated Fig13 joint/fork interpretation superseded by modern genus morphology; omitted. Ordovician Trenton Wisconsin not Silurian.
WHITFIELD1894.inspection: Personally inspected whole original PlateXI rendered2000px; only11-12 inform candidate habit. Adjacent Buthograptus/Callithamnopsis/Primicorallina drawings excluded.

LODUCA2011.title: LoDuca, Melchin and Verbruggen2011 Complex noncalcified macroalgae from the Silurian of Cornwallis Island
LODUCA2011.notes: Original fulltext downloaded/read. Revised Chaetocladus architecture undivided cylindrical main axis and unbranched laterals in whorls; C.plumula remains cited from Ordovician Wisconsin. C.capitatus species measurements and enlargedcrown are NOT imported. Confirms correction to1894 putativeforks.
LODUCA2011.inspection: Actual primary text read. Morphological pixel basis remains originalC.plumulaPlateXI, not C.capitatus image.
